title: Wieland–Miescher ketone
goal: A Robinson annulation made asymmetric: Michael addition, a proline-catalysed intramolecular aldol and dehydration give a steroid building block.

problemSets.title: Michael addition
problemSets.conceptInOneLine: A 1,3-dione enolate adds to methyl vinyl ketone and builds a quaternary carbon.
problemSets.conceptCard:
The *Wieland–Miescher ketone* (1950) is a bicyclic enone with an angular methyl group: the A and B rings of many steroids and terpenoids. It is made by a **Robinson annulation** of 2-methylcyclohexane-1,3-dione with methyl vinyl ketone.

The C–H between two C=O groups is very acidic (pKa about 5), so a **catalytic** amount of KOH is enough. The enolate adds to the far end of the enone (**conjugate addition**), and water protonates the new, more basic enolate, returning hydroxide.

- the new carbon is **quaternary**: methyl, side chain and two ring carbonyls
- the two ring carbonyls are **mirror images** of each other (enantiotopic): the next ring can close onto either, and that choice decides which enantiomer forms

setItems.whyThisOne: Warm-up: the same four-arrow conjugate addition from a cyclohexanone enolate.
The real thing: a dione so acidic that hydroxide is only a catalyst.

problemSets.title: Intramolecular aldol via a proline enamine
problemSets.conceptInOneLine: Proline makes an enamine and delivers a proton to one of two mirror-image carbonyls: the first asymmetric organocatalysis.
problemSets.conceptCard:
In 1971 two industrial groups, **Hajos and Parrish** at Hoffmann-La Roche and **Eder, Sauer and Wiechert** at Schering, found that a few mol % of the amino acid **(S)-proline** closes the triketone with high enantioselectivity.

Proline does two jobs:

- its **secondary amine** condenses with the open methyl ketone to give an **enamine**, a neutral enol equivalent (as in Carbonyl addition)
- its **carboxylic acid** protonates the carbonyl oxygen as the enamine attacks it

The ring-closing aldol is the **ee-deciding step**. The acid hydrogen-bonds to one of the two ring carbonyls in a chair-like transition state (the *Houk–List model*), so that carbonyl reacts much faster: the (S)-ketone forms in about 70 % ee (93 % for the five-membered Hajos–Parrish analogue). Hydrolysis then releases proline.

The app does not check stereochemistry yet: either ring carbonyl is accepted, and the text explains which one is chosen.

setItems.whyThisOne: Warm-up: an enamine from a ketone and a secondary amine.
Proline picks the open ketone, and its acid group shuttles the protons.
The step that decides the enantiomer, then hydrolysis frees the catalyst.

problemSets.title: Dehydration to the enone
problemSets.conceptInOneLine: The ketol loses water through an enol in acid, keeping the stereocentre set in the aldol.
problemSets.conceptCard:
The aldol product is a **β-hydroxy ketone** (a ketol). Losing water gives the conjugated enone.

- in **base**, an enolate pushes out hydroxide: **E1cB**, as in the Robinson annulation
- in **acid** (TsOH, Dean–Stark), an **enol** pushes out water from the protonated OH

For the asymmetric synthesis, acid is the safer choice: base can also run the aldol **backwards** to the achiral triketone and erode the enantiomeric excess. The quaternary stereocentre takes no part in the dehydration, so its configuration survives.

setItems.whyThisOne: Warm-up: aldol and E1cB dehydration in base.
The same dehydration in acid, through the enol.

problemSets.title: Checkpoint
problemSets.conceptInOneLine: The four steps of the Wieland–Miescher synthesis, shuffled, with their names hidden.
problemSets.conceptCard:
The four reactions of this track in random order and without their names. For each one, ask:

- which C–H or N–H is acidic, and which base or acid is in the flask?
- which carbonyl reacts, and why that one?
- where does proline's carboxylic acid give or take a proton?
- which step decides the enantiomer, and which steps leave it alone?

setItems.whyThisOne: A catalytic base and a conjugate addition.
Which ketone does the amine choose?
Four arrows at once: enamine, new bond and proton delivery.
